title: Terms and Conditions of Service: Rate Schedule Changes Under an Electric Service Agreement
content:
**Terms and conditions of service, Lakeshore Power & Light Company: moving an Electric Service Agreement to another rate schedule**

**1. Right to change.** The customer may move an Electric Service Agreement that is active or notice pending to another schedule of the same customer type (residential or business) whose entry requirements the service address meets. The same demand, communicating-meter and vehicle tests apply as when an agreement is opened.

**2. Agreements that cannot be changed.** A change requested on a closed, disconnected or pending start agreement is not made. The company reads the agreement's status from its own records.

**3. Lockout period.** A schedule change is accepted only when the rate change lockout period has elapsed since the current schedule's effective date. The lockout is the value set by the current schedule. Months are counted as calendar months from the rate effective date, and when the target month is shorter, the boundary falls on its last day. A request made on the boundary day is accepted; a request made before it is not.

**4. Return within bill protection.** The lockout does not apply when a customer still inside the bill-protection period of Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service or Schedule REV Residential Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use Service returns to Schedule RS Residential Standard Service, or when a customer still inside the bill-protection period of Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service returns to Schedule GS Small General Service.

**5. Effective date.** The new schedule takes effect on the first day after the billing period end of the most recent regular bill, and that date becomes the agreement's rate effective date. No bill is recalculated retroactively.

## Lockout boundary (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical figures for illustration only:* a current schedule whose lockout is 6 months, and a rate effective date of 31 August 2025. Six calendar months later is February 2026, which has no 31st, so the boundary falls on 28 February 2026.

| Request date | Lockout elapsed? |
|---|---|
| 27 February 2026 (the day before the boundary) | no; the change is not accepted |
| 28 February 2026 (the boundary day) | yes; the change is accepted |

## Effective date (hypothetical)

*Hypothetical:* the most recent regular bill covered a billing period ending on 14 May. An accepted change takes effect on 15 May, which is written as the new rate effective date; the bill for the period ending 14 May stays as issued.
